1.w: Simeon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, To those having obtained a faith equally precious with ours, through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ:

2.w: Grace and peace be multiplied to you⁺ in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord.

3.w: Accordingly, His divine power has given to us all things toward life and godliness, through the knowledge of the One having called us [by His] own glory and excellence,

4.w: through which He has given to us the precious and magnificent promises, so that through these you⁺ might become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption in the world in evil desire.

5.w: Now also for this very [reason], having brought in all diligence, supply in your⁺ faith virtue, and in virtue knowledge,

6.w: and in knowledge self-control, and in self-control perseverance, and in perseverance godliness,

7.w: and in godliness brotherly affection, and in brotherly affection love.

8.w: For these things being in you⁺ and abounding make [you] neither idle nor unfruitful in regard to the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

9.w: For in whomever these things are not present, he is blind, being shortsighted, having received forgetfulness of the cleansing [from] his former sins.

10.w: Therefore, brothers, be diligent, rather, to make your⁺ calling and election sure. For [in] doing these things, never at any time shall you⁺ stumble.

11.w: For in this way the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly supplied to you⁺.

12.w: Therefore I will be ready always to remind you⁺ concerning these things, though knowing [them] and having been strengthened in the truth being present.

13.w: Now I esteem it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you⁺ up in a reminder,

14.w: knowing that the putting off of my tabernacle is soon, as also our Lord Jesus Christ made clear to me.

15.w: And I will be diligent also for you⁺ to have at every time after my departure these things, to make a lasting remembrance.

16.w: For we did not make known to you⁺ the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ having followed after cleverly devised myths, but having been eyewitnesses of His majesty.

17.w: For having received honor and glory from God the Father, a voice such as follows was brought to Him by the Majestic Glory: “This is My Son, My beloved, in whom I was well pleased.”

18.w: And we heard this voice having been brought out of heaven, being with Him in the holy mountain.

19.w: And we have the more certain prophetic word, to which you⁺ do well taking heed, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until this day shall have dawned and the morning star shall have arisen in your⁺ hearts,

20.w: knowing this first, that every prophecy of Scripture is not of its own interpretation.

21.w: For not by the will of man was prophecy brought forth at any time, but being carried by the Holy Spirit, men spoke from God.
